text_blocks.answer: The opening line of Homer's Iliad is: "μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος" (traditionally transcribed in lowercase as μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ πηληϊάδεω ἀχιλῆοσ), which translates to: "Sing, goddess, the anger of Achilles, Peleus' son".⁠The Open University +1

items.answer: μῆνιν (mēnin): Noun (accusative singular feminine) — wrath or anger. Placed first for dramatic emphasis.⁠The Guardian +1
ἄειδε (aeide): Verb (present active imperative, 2nd person singular) — sing (as in invoking the Muse).
θεὰ (thea): Noun (vocative singular feminine) — goddess (referring to the Muse).⁠The Open University +1
Πηληϊάδεω (Peleiadeō): Patronymic noun (genitive singular masculine, Homeric form) —
Ἀχιλῆος (Akhilēos): Proper noun (genitive singular masculine, Homeric form) — of Achilles.⁠The Open University +1
